messages:
Anna (Support): FYI ticket #INC-8421 — ACME asked for clarity on our data retention defaults and wants an immediate legal-hold on all user data for acct_acme_77. They say they have a regulator audit next week. Can we confirm timelines?
Charlie (Infra): Got the ticket. Our default hosted retention is 30 days for request logs + 90 days for full audit bundle (config + logs), unless a custom retention is set.
Anna (Support): Customer is pushing for 7 years preservation and immediate suspension of automatic deletion. They also asked whether KMS keys are rotated/deleted on customer request.
Eve (SecOps): Important: we can't delete KMS material on demand if they need a legal hold. But they can request key export if they have entitlement; HSM-export is limited. Need to know whether ACME uses our managed keys or brought their own CMK (customer-managed).
Anna (Support): ACME said they use "Redwood-managed KMS" when they onboarded.
Ben (Legal): From a legal perspective, if a formal legal hold is requested we should flip retention to an immutable hold and disable garbage collection. That requires an internal sign-off (legal + security). Also need to record hold reason and owner.
Charlie (Infra): Operationally we can apply a per-account retention override. Example config we would push to the retention service:
```json
{"account_id":"acct_acme_77","retention_days":2555,"immutable_hold":true,"preserve_audit_logs":true,"kms_key":"managed/redwood/global/region1"}
```
This will stop async deletion jobs and preserve KV/cache dumps for the retention window.
Eve (SecOps): Note: immutable_hold=true will also prevent the automated key-rotation daemon from purging old key versions, but it does not change crypto policy for HSM. If they ask to rotate or destroy keys, we must escalate to infra + legal and get a signed authorization.
Anna (Support): ACME wants confirmation of timeline — they need an SOC-style attestation that data will be preserved immediately and that we can provide audit logs for 7 years.
Ben (Legal): We can approve a legal hold pending signed request via their legal contact. Once signed, we will: 1) create immutable hold, 2) set retention_days=2555 (7y), 3) tag all related storage buckets and audit logs as preserved.
Charlie (Infra): ETA to apply hold after approval: ~30 min to run policy job and verify. Exports of historical logs: we can generate a full audit bundle (S3 export) — expect 2-4 hours for a full account export depending on size.
Anna (Support): I'll ask the customer to send signed hold request to legal@redwood.com and include ticket INC-8421.
Eve (SecOps): Also tell them: deletion API (DELETE /v1/accounts/{id}/data) will be blocked while immutable_hold is set. Example curl we use for ad-hoc deletion (for reference, NOT applicable under hold):
```bash
curl -X DELETE https://api.redwood.ai/v1/accounts/acct_acme_77/data \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
```
Anna (Support): I'll draft a customer-facing response summarizing legal steps, timelines, and the KMS constraints. Putting Ben + Eve + Charlie on the thread for sign-off.
Ben (Legal): I can sign once they send the signed hold.
Charlie (Infra): I'll prep the automation runbook and a manual rollback plan (in case of mis-tag).
Eve (SecOps): Flagging compliance-bot to create an internal audit ticket.
compliance-bot: Created internal case CB-9091 for retention hold workflow.
Anna (Support): Thanks — I'll update INC-8421 and ping when signed docs arrive. :thumbsup:
